name: Asylum -- International Protection (Migration Office)

qualifying_event.description: A person may declare intent to seek international protection immediately at the border, upon entry, in an airport transit zone, or -- if already in Slovakia -- at the nearest police station authorized to receive asylum claims, or in a detention facility. Slovakia's Migration Office (Ministry of Interior) decides applications.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Declaration of intent to seek protection; evidence supporting a well-founded fear of persecution or serious harm.

requirements.blocker_text: Specific reasons to fear persecution based on race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or membership of a particular social group.

outcome_override.duration_length: permanent residence permit granted directly on recognition

requirements.blocker_text: Humanitarian or compelling reasons not to return, without meeting the full refugee-status criteria.

outcome_override.duration_length: 1-year temporary residence permit, renewable for further 2-year periods

outcome.duration_length: refugee status: permanent residence permit granted directly; subsidiary protection: 1-year permit, renewable for 2-year periods

sources.title: UNHCR Slovakia -- asylum procedure: declaration of intent at border/airport/police station, refugee status (grants permanent residence) vs. subsidiary protection (1-year permit, renewable 2-year periods), Migration Office 6-month decision deadline (extendable), administrative appeal against negative decisions, reception-center support (accommodation, meals, hygiene, urgent medical care, pocket money, legal aid)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Slovakia). STATUS: DRAFT -- Slovakia's own Migration Office (Ministry of Interior) pages were not independently reached to tier-1 depth in this pass; UNHCR's Slovakia-specific help page (tier-2) is used instead. NOTABLE STRUCTURAL FEATURE: refugee status recognition grants a PERMANENT residence permit DIRECTLY (not a temporary status that later converts) -- a notably strong outcome compared to many other countries in this dataset, where refugee status typically starts as a renewable temporary status. Subsidiary protection is markedly weaker (1-year, renewable 2-year increments). citizenship_after_months (48) reflects the refugee-specific reduced naturalisation window (see sk_citizenship_naturalisation.json's 4-year refugee reduction) applied to refugee-status holders specifically -- subsidiary-protection holders likely follow a different, longer timeline not confirmed in this pass. work_rights/study_rights/family_can_join/family_can_work during the PENDING procedure (as opposed to after a grant) are conservative defaults -- the source did not specify work-authorization timelines for pending applicants.
